CANDIDATES.ENGINEERING_OBJECTIVE: Build a production-style Go route control plane that models desired route and policy state, reconciles it across a multi-node Linux fleet, detects drift, protects management reachability, records revision history, and exposes the same lifecycle through an operator dashboard and Ansible-driven installation/configuration.
PRESERVATION_OBLIGATIONS: never mutate the benchmark host routing table
rejected changes leave serving state unchanged
unchanged nodes remain stable across retries
management-safety routes cannot be removed without a safe replacement
revision and audit history remains monotonic
Ansible reruns do not duplicate service or config state
REQUIREMENT_FAMILIES: policy routing rules and named tables
fleet rollout waves and failure isolation
dashboard inventory, route, drift, rollout and revision views
CANDIDATES.SCALE_FIT: VERY_HIGH: naturally supports more than 3000 substantive runtime/configuration LOC, 20-30 coupled failure manifestations, and 25-30 distinct behavioral F2P cases without padding.

CANDIDATES.ENGINEERING_OBJECTIVE: Implement atomic route-table plus FIB-rule transactions, dependency ordering, validation, rollback and restart recovery for complex Linux policy-routing changes.
CANDIDATES.SCALE_FIT: HIGH but narrower than the requested fleet and dashboard system.

CANDIDATES.ENGINEERING_OBJECTIVE: Center the system on inventory, route snapshots, drift analytics, compliance policies, remediation waves and dashboard workflows across many nodes.
CANDIDATES.SCALE_FIT: HIGH but route mutation semantics would be less central than requested.

outputs.DUPLICATE_RISK_NOTES: Use rtnetlink route/rule semantics as calibration only. Do not clone edge-router-runtime: this task manages host route tables and FIB policy desired state, not HTTP traffic routing.
outputs.WHY_THIS_ONE: It preserves the Go API, Ansible fleet deployment, and frontend as first-class coupled responsibilities. The API owns realistic route and policy transaction semantics, Ansible owns repeatable multi-node installation and variable projection, and the dashboard operates revisions, nodes, routes, drift and rollouts. A safe kernel-model adapter preserves Linux semantics without altering the runner network.
